results.title: Mixture-of-Experts inference on Apple Silicon
results.content: A mixture-of-experts model activates a small fraction of its weights for any given token, which means the remainder has no reason to occupy memory. Keeping the expert pool on SSD and holding a few experts per layer in a bounded slot cache is enough to run models far larger than resident memory. The cost is paid in prompt processing rather than in decoding.

results.title: Metal kernels for quantized GEMV
results.content: Quantized matrix-vector products on the GPU are bound by memory bandwidth rather than arithmetic. Splitting the reduction across threadgroups helps once the context is long enough that a single threadgroup per query head leaves the machine idle.
Prompt processing runs a chunk of tokens through each layer together, so an expert is read once for the whole chunk rather than once per token that wanted it.
